## Get started

1. Download and extract the ZIP into a folder in your personal course project.
2. Read the questions and data dictionary in `actg175-student.html`.
3. Create your own R Markdown or Quarto report beside the supplied `data/` folder.
   A report template is not provided.
4. Organize your report by question and subpart number, showing the code that
   generates each table, plot, and numerical result.

Part 1 analyzes the supplied clinical trial data. Part 2 uses simulation to
estimate power and plan sample sizes and recruitment for a new study.
The questions contain the complete computing and submission requirements.

## What to submit

Submit your `.Rmd` or `.qmd` source and matching HTML to your private GitHub
repository, with course staff access as described in
[Session 2](../course/session02/lab.qmd). The report should render without
unexpected errors or warnings.

Keep `results/simulation-results.rds` locally for your analysis and the requested
MD5 checks; it does not need to be submitted.

## Supplied files

The ZIP contains exactly three files:

| File | Purpose |
|:--|:--|
| [actg175-student.html](files/actg175-student.html) | Questions, instructions, and data dictionary |
| [data/baseline.csv](files/data/baseline.csv) | Participant-level baseline data |
| [data/cd4-visits.csv](files/data/cd4-visits.csv) | CD4 measurements by visit |

The questions HTML can also be read offline after extracting the ZIP.
